body:
# v0.1.7: investigate the retained-history measured-operation slowdown against v0.1.6

> **Status:** Investigation. No product change is proposed here, and nothing in this
> issue is a claim about the 217-row Stage 6 lane. Opened from the re-check recorded
> in [`stage-6-recheck-20260920T000000Z`](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/main/docs/roadmap/0.1/0.1.7/evidence/stage-6-recheck-20260920T000000Z/README.md) §4.

## 1. The observation

The retained-history lane is the **only** place in the tree with a recorded v0.1.6
comparator, and time there is a **one-sided tripwire** (owner ruling 6,
[`retained-history-storage.md`](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/main/docs/roadmap/0.1/0.1.7/retained-history-storage.md) §8):

> Passing the time comparison proves nothing. **Failing it proves a flaw.**

`history-stride10`, 17 states, the same corpus pins on both sides:

| stride-10 (17 states) | v0.1.6 (recorded) | ours | ratio |
| --- | --: | --: | --: |
| measured operation — their Commit sum / our Σ 17 named children | **11.371 s** (median 564.3 ms) | **32.566 s** (median 1,564.1 ms) | **2.86×** (median 2.77×) |
| end-to-end wall | 98.0 s (exec 59.7 + per-state install 18.6 + commit 11.4) | 45.0 s invocation | **0.46× — we are 2.2× faster** |

Larger tiers, incomplete on our side: v0.1.6 recorded Commit sums of 24.815 s at 53
states and 64.108 s at 157; our stride-3 and stride-1 runs retained **wall only**
(97.9 s and 289.5 s) and no operation sum, so no ratio can be computed for them.
`history-stride1` has no retained receipt at all.

**So the finding is narrow and specific:** we win the wall and lose the measured
operation, by ~2.9×, on the one axis where a v0.1.6 number exists.

## 2. What is established, and what is not

Established:

- Both sides measured the same selection (17 states, `range(1,158,10) ∪ {157}`) over
  the same corpus pins; canonical content is byte-identical (the storage gate
  reproduced v0.1.6's canonical totals).
- Our figure is the sum of the 17 per-state children published by the product's own
  telemetry (`construct + build_filesystem + save`), not a root that includes the
  harness's untimed corpus reads (owner ruling 2).
- The storage side is a pass at all three sizes: 49,053,696 / 61,767,680 / 80,273,408 B
  apparent against 49,344,512 / 64,024,576 / 83,947,520 B allocated.

**Not** established, and each of these can move the ratio:

- The two timers do not measure the same composition. Ours includes C1 content
  construction and the tree update; v0.1.6's Commit sat inside a container with its
  `exec` (59.7 s) and per-state fixture install (18.6 s) **outside** the Commit.
- v0.1.6's numbers are **cited, not re-run**, on a machine state that is not
  described; ours were taken at load ~5 with a competing `cargo` process, and the
  same configuration measured 64.2 s and 90.3 s on repeat in the verification phase
  (a 40 % spread).
- The lane runs `LAYERFS_CONSTRUCTION_WORKERS=1` by acceptance rule; the v0.1.6
  campaign ran under the container runtime and this constraint did not apply to it.
  This is a **declared difference**, not a defect, and it must be quantified rather
  than argued.
- No per-state decomposition of our 32.566 s exists (how much is construct, how much
  is tree update, how much is `begin_save`/`accept`/`finish`), so the difference is
  currently attributed to nothing.

## 3. Hypotheses, each with the measurement that would settle it

| # | hypothesis | what settles it |
| --: | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Composition** — the two timers bracket different work, and most of the 21.2 s gap is work v0.1.6 never timed | Split our per-state child into `content` / `build` / `storage.begin` / `storage.finish` (the spans already exist in the timing tree) and reconcile against v0.1.6's Commit composition |
| 2 | **Codec cost** — `GROUP_LEVEL` 1 → 19 and the 16 MiB encode workspace raised encode CPU | Re-run stride-10 with the group level at 1 (a matched pair differing by one constant); the commit-cadence effect of that change is already measured in the re-check above |
| 3 | **Worker count** — one construction worker versus the reference's runtime default | Run the same selection with the declared worker rule and with the reference's worker count as a **declared, labelled diagnostic**, never as a gate arm |
| 4 | **Similarity index and chunk cursor** — the persisted cross-save index and the C1 predecessor path add per-object work | Counters already exist (`delta.trials`, `delta.ineligible_candidates`, `delta.reused`); attribute the 38,230 trials against the codec's own instrumented CPU |
| 5 | **Cache state** — our states read the corpus untimed while the reference installed each state inside its work wall | Declare and enforce the same cache contract on both sides, or state plainly that the surfaces cannot be matched |

## 4. Acceptance — what closing this issue requires

1. A **per-phase decomposition** of the stride-10 operation on the frozen selection,
   with every span named and the arithmetic reconciled (residual stated, not smoothed).
2. An attribution of the difference to **named mechanisms**, each measured, not
   inferred; hypotheses that fail are recorded as falsified.
3. A disposition, with an owner ruling where one is needed: fix, accept-and-record
   with the reason, or re-rule the tripwire.
4. If a product change follows, the ordinary rules apply: iterate on stride-10,
   confirm on stride-3, **never optimize `history-stride1`**, and no constant,
   threshold, buffer or policy value changed because of a stride-1 number.

## 5. Boundaries

- **No 217-row claim is touched.** `CONTRACT.md` D1 freezes `structural-complexity`
  and forbids pairing a C1/C2 family with a v0.1.6 family; this issue is inside the
  retained-history lane, whose time axis is published, labelled and never
  gate-deciding.
- **No product change without a ruling.** This issue starts as an investigation.
- **No new performance claim.** A speed-up would prove nothing here; only the
  removal of an unexplained slowdown is the goal.
- Wall and CPU on both sides are indicative: the machine was not quiet for our runs,
  and the reference figures are cited rather than re-measured.

## 6. Evidence

- Our stride-10 phase receipt, per-state spans and counters, read from the retained
  run directory: [`stage-6-recheck-20260920T000000Z`](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/main/docs/roadmap/0.1/0.1.7/evidence/stage-6-recheck-20260920T000000Z/README.md) §4.
- Tier results and memory: [`stage-6-history-188d-20260920T000000Z/ALL-THREE-TIERS.md`](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/main/docs/roadmap/0.1/0.1.7/evidence/stage-6-history-188d-20260920T000000Z/ALL-THREE-TIERS.md).
- Verification walls and their declared ceilings: [`.../VERIFICATION.md`](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/main/docs/roadmap/0.1/0.1.7/evidence/stage-6-history-188d-20260920T000000Z/VERIFICATION.md).
- The v0.1.6 record: [`issue153-retained-history-report.md`](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/main/docs/roadmap/0.1/0.1.6/evidence/issue153-retained-history-report.md) §1.
- Ruling 6 and the lane's budgets: [`retained-history-storage.md`](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/main/docs/roadmap/0.1/0.1.7/retained-history-storage.md) §8, §11.1.
title: v0.1.7: investigate the retained-history measured-operation slowdown against v0.1.6 (2.86x on stride-10)
